findings.reason: The rewrite of src/user/invite.js stores groupsToJoin with JSON.stringify but passes that stored string directly to groups.join, which treats it as a group name rather than joining the invitation's groups. deleteInvitationKeyByToken calls new Set(tokens).map(...), which throws because Set has no map method, preventing token cleanup. The rewrite also makes verification reject a valid token when an optional email differs and never stores the required invitation:uid:<uid>:invited:<email> reference. These defects remain in the final patch.

The controller change calls deleteInvitationKey(userData.email || userData.token) only for token registrations. When a registrant enters an email different from the invited email, this selects the unrelated entered email and leaves the used token and invitation references behind. It also leaves invitations uncleared when someone registers with an invited email without supplying a token. Neither behavior was repaired.

run_review.reason: The final patch omits the required client-side change that copies the URL token into the registration form. Its invitation implementation also passes JSON-serialized group data to groups.join without parsing it, and token cleanup throws because Set has no map method. Registration cleanup uses the entered email instead of the invitation token when both are present, so a different entered email leaves the used invitation intact. The verifier reported failures in the invitation tests; although the overall evaluation timed out, the final patch independently shows these core defects.

That helper removes inviter references across all inviting users and deletes every token associated with the email, so an admin action specifying one inviter can also delete other inviters' invitations. This is an overly broad destructive scope; no execution of that path is observed.
